summary:
The design is sound in substance. It changes test code only, every assertion was spiked on b719e31, and both kill sets are disjoint and measured (A fails exactly 3 rows; B fails exactly the admin-share Fact).

Checked by reading the repro's regex reader (LastAccessGatesAssertionsTests.cs:39-67, :112-128): the planned forms satisfy both checks.
- (a): the [Theory] unit carries `AddAttributes(`, `Offline` or `0x80000`, `LastAccessAsked` and `Assert.`. The reader does not split units at [InlineData].
- (b): `Assert.Equal(0, above.LastAccessAsked)` sits in the same unit as `localhost`/`Loopback`.
- So case 14 should pass. Running the reader against the edited tree is still owed (`eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions.Tests.csproj`).

The one major problem: the slice's real criteria, (a') and (b'), are mutant kills. The design discharges them only by hand edits in an uncommitted scratch copy. That breaks the project's CC-004 check. It also leaves "mutants never touch the worktree" as something the builder must remember, after the survey already broke it once. The SL-102 repro cannot stand in, because it reads source text: the StalledShareTests asserts alone (`RemotePath`) satisfy (b), whether or not any default-suite assertion exists.

Minor problems:
- The rationale says engine stages run as SYSTEM. Only the Sandbox does.
- The rationale says PINNED and UNPINNED are missing from Kernel32. Kernel32.cs:31-32 defines both.
- Two of the design's code lines do not compile: a static AddAttributes is called through an instance, and a uint is mixed with FileAttributes under `&`/`==` precedence.
- The only default-suite guard of the remote gate is placed inside a removable workaround's Fact. The reason given for not writing a dedicated Fact ("unspiked") is contradicted by the investigation's probe, which measured that scan.
- The count-only oracle cannot tell which folder was left out.

What breaks if a must-verify precondition fails:
1. If the admin share does not answer (admin shares off, a non-Administrators account, or UAC remote restrictions on loopback for local or Microsoft accounts, per KB951016), the Fact `continue`s and mutant B survives the default suite with nothing visible. The text-only SL-102 repro still passes, so acceptance and protection come apart. The design already files this.
2. If a mutant run contaminates the worktree, the build commits a disabled M6 gate. Under B that means SetFileInformationByHandle on every share folder. Only an end-of-run `git diff` that someone has to remember stands in the way, which is why M1 asks for a committed driver.

findings.claim:
The slice's defining criteria are mutant kills: survey (a') and (b'), plus the design's material case 'catch a cloud bit dropped from the mask'. The design discharges all of them only by hand-applied edits in an uncommitted `git archive` scratch copy. No committed command exists that validate can rerun.

This breaks accepted check CC-004 (cases must be backed by a committed, runnable command, not scratch probes). It also leaves the design's own must-verify precondition, 'mutant runs never contaminate the real worktree', as something to remember. The survey already broke it once: a relative path in a hand script wrote mutant B into the worktree's Scanner.cs.

The committed acceptance check cannot stand in. The SL-102 repro reads source text, and the StalledShareTests asserts alone satisfy its (b) check (`RemotePath` plus `Assert.Equal(0, result.LastAccessAsked)`). So the repro goes green whether or not the default suite kills mutant B. Lesson #412 (SL-100's uncommitted, unreproducible mutant script) is the same failure.
findings.evidence: Design cases 'catch a cloud bit dropped from the mask', 'turn the default suite red when the attribute gate is removed' and 'turn the default suite red when the remote gate is removed' each have the check 'In a git-archive scratch copy with absolute paths ... remove that bit ...'. Survey incident: '[IO.File]::WriteAllText with a relative path wrote the mutation into the WORKTREE's src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/Scanner.cs'. Repro regex ScansAShare includes `\bRemotePath\b` (LastAccessGatesAssertionsTests.cs:60-61).

Design contract 'Opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK run': 'Engine stages run as SYSTEM and cannot map the share (error 1312).' Its outside_claims entry sources this to spike smb-loopback-assertion-catches-remote-mutant-in-sandbox, whose RUN 1 was 'as SYSTEM (the plan's identity)' inside Windows Sandbox.

findings.fix: Restate the rationale in the contract, the key decision and the outside_claims entry. The SMB-LOOPBACK run is a person's because New-SmbMapping changes machine state and stages may not do it (#120, CC-006). It needs Windows 11 24H2+. In the Sandbox, SYSTEM additionally gets error 1312. Keep filed_for_later unchanged.

findings.claim:
Two lines of the Theory, as the design writes them, do not compile.
1. `tree.AddAttributes(off, attribute)` calls a static method through an instance (CS0176). TempTree.AddAttributes is `public static`.
2. The precondition `Scans.Listing(root)["off"].Attributes & attribute == attribute` mixes `uint` (RawEntry.Attributes, DirectoryReader.cs:15) with `FileAttributes`. C# precedence also makes it `a & (b == b)`.

The builder will notice at once. But the design is the contract code review checks against, and the spike's evidence used the static form `TempTree.AddAttributes(off, ...)`.
findings.evidence: Design component 'Cloud-attribute Theory': 'then tree.AddAttributes(off, attribute)' and 'Precondition: Scans.Listing(root)["off"].Attributes & attribute == attribute'. RawEntry: `public uint Attributes;` (src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/DirectoryReader.cs:15).

quote.text: public static void AddAttributes(string path, FileAttributes attributes) =>

findings.claim:
The PINNED case's 'why' says 'PINNED is in the mask but missing from Kernel32's named table, so a dropped bit here is the likeliest silent regression'. The prior_art entry repeats it ('PINNED and UNPINNED are absent from that table, which is why the Theory rows use hex literals').

Kernel32.cs defines FILE_ATTRIBUTE_PINNED and FILE_ATTRIBUTE_UNPINNED, and Scanner.cs:144 builds the mask from them by name. The real reason hex literals are needed is that System.IO.FileAttributes has no Pinned or Unpinned member. The 'likeliest regression' ranking rests on a false premise. It changes nothing in the build, but it corrupts the record a later slice would read.
findings.fix: Change the case's 'why' and the prior_art note to say: the rows use hex literals because System.IO.FileAttributes lacks Pinned and Unpinned, and because rows must not be derived from the code under test. Every bit row is justified by the spike's single-bit kills, not by a missing constant.

findings.claim:
After this slice, the only default-suite guard of M6's remote gate lives inside AScanThroughThisPcsAdminShareRefusesInsideTheStoreAndSkipsItFromAbove. That Fact belongs to the wcifs-layer-store KnownWorkarounds entry, which is removable by design (Q-186).

The only check that the assertion still exists is the SL-102 repro in tests/bugs, which sits outside FsAnalyser.slnx and never runs by default. Lesson #411 records exactly this: a guard lost with every required check green. Retiring or reshaping the workaround's test would silently drop the remote-gate kill.

The design's reason for not writing a dedicated Fact is that it is 'unspiked'. The investigation's probe measured exactly that scan: a plain, cloud-bit-free b-tree through \\localhost\C$ and \\127.0.0.1\C$ with default options read asked 0, kept 0 unmutated and 4/4 under mutant B.
findings.evidence: Design taste_disagreements: 'A dedicated Fact would be clearer about its subject, but it is unspiked and adds a second admin-share scan.' Investigation probe table: 'b-tree via \\localhost\C$ | 0/0 | 0/0 | 4/4'. The Fact's options are Planted(tree), with ContainerLayerStorePath (ContainerLayerStoreTests.cs:45-50).
findings.fix: Add a LastAccessTests Fact. It scans a plain TempTree (a\one.txt, b\one.txt, b\inner\two.txt, no attributes) through `\\{host}\{drive}$\...` for both hosts, with the same `Directory.Exists` continue. It asserts Completed, Bytes 4 and LastAccessAsked == 0 (the probe-measured shape). Keep or drop the four ContainerLayerStoreTests lines; either way the remote gate's subject test no longer depends on a workaround's lifecycle.

findings.claim:
Asked == 3 shows that ONE of {off, off\inner} was left out. It does not show WHICH. Suppose the gate is shifted one level, so a folder is judged by its parent's attributes (a plausible refactor if the decision moves to push time, when the parent's listing is appended). Then `off` is asked and `off\inner` is not, which also gives 3. The Theory passes.

The design's case 'still count what is under a cloud-marked folder' claims a mark carried down to children reads Asked 2. That holds only when both folders are skipped, not under a shift.
findings.evidence: Scanner.cs:199 decides each popped folder from its own listed attributes. Design case: 'A change that skips the marked subtree, or carries the mark down to children, would read Asked 2 or Bytes below 4'.
findings.fix: Give `off` two plain subfolders (off\i1\x.txt, off\i2\y.txt). The correct count is then 4 (root, a, i1, i2), a shifted gate gives 3 and mutant A gives 5. Re-measure the expected Asked under both TEMPs before pinning it.

dimensions_checked.result:
Two findings: m1 (the engine was assumed to run as SYSTEM; that is the Sandbox's identity, not this PC's engine) and m3 (PINNED and UNPINNED were said to be missing from Kernel32; Kernel32.cs:31-32 defines them).

Also overstated, though not raised: the reason given for rejecting OverrideQueryError ('rewrites every Query, could hit the size probe'). The override is a per-instance property (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:131), and ProbePass makes its own guards (ProbePass.cs:143). 'Call numbering unchecked' remains a valid reason on its own.

The cited Old New Thing claim was checked. The source says 'Merely opening the file will not recall it ... GetFileInformationByHandle ... without triggering a recall', so the citation is supported.

m5: the count-only oracle cannot tell which folder was left out, so a gate shifted one level survives.

The RECALL_ON_* bits, a root that itself carries cloud bits, and a PC with admin shares off are already filed. I agree with the reasons given (user mode cannot set the RECALL bits; the root case is a separate attribute source).

M1: the mutant-kill evidence and the no-contamination invariant are held by remembering, with no committed driver.

m4: the remote gate's only default-suite guard sits in a workaround's Fact, and its only existence check is a tests/bugs repro outside the slnx.

None material. The three-row Theory is justified by the measured per-bit kills.

The `LastAccessKept == 0` asserts on the share scans can never fire on their own. CountListingOpen increments Kept only after Asked (Scanner.cs:336-339), and Asked == 0 is asserted first. So the design's claim that Kept 'pins the actual SetFileInformationByHandle' adds no kill. At one line each it is harmless and left alone.

The design rightly adds no Stryker runner, no new seam and no fitness rule.

m2: the design's literal code calls a static TempTree.AddAttributes through an instance, and its precondition mixes uint and FileAttributes with the wrong precedence.

The acceptance csproj name `.Tests.csproj` was verified to exist (tests/bugs/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions.Tests.csproj).

None. Each Theory row's listing precondition turns a filesystem that drops the bit into a red row rather than a vacuous pass. The admin-share `continue` path (vacuous kill) is filed for later.

If the admin share does not answer, the Fact passes doing nothing and mutant B survives. The KB951016 UAC remote restrictions ('helps prevent against loopback attacks') make this depend on account type and Administrators membership, not only on a sharing switch. The design's filed item names 'a PC or account', so this is not raised again.

None. The three-row Theory is a superset of the slice's Offline Fact. The SMB-LOOPBACK `LastAccessAsked == 0` is added as the slice asks. Its proof is filed as the person's check, matching the survey's checked_by: person and lesson #420. Scanner.cs stays byte-identical, consistent with the investigation's cause (a test gap, not a scanner fault).

M1 (CC-004: case checks rest on uncommitted scratch procedures).

CC-005 traced:
- The Theory reaches the gate. TempTree redirects out of C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (TempTree.cs:62-76). The environment's sync roots do not cover %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. Local NTFS fails FileRemoteProtocolInfo with error 87, so _keepLastAccess is true.
- The admin-share Fact reaches the gate (shareHosts = 2, measured).

Fitness checks:
- CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped (fitness.yaml:129-137) and the %SystemRoot%\Temp route rule (:1146-1161) are respected: no Skip, no Trait, no GetTempPath.
- LastAccessRuleCorpusTests pins only LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests (:94-97).
- The RigLock rule (:802) is untouched.

Read the repro's reader: the design's forms satisfy (a) and (b), so case 14 should pass. It still has to be run.

Weakness: (b) is satisfied by the opt-in StalledShareTests text alone, so the repro cannot show default-suite protection. Only the mutant runs can, which is why M1 matters.

The kill sets were measured: A fails 3 rows and B fails 1 Fact (873/873 unmutated) under both TEMPs.

None. The change is test-only. The OFFLINE, PINNED and UNPINNED bits are set on TempTree folders that are deleted afterwards (spike: 0 leftovers over 10 runs), and per the cited Old New Thing post, metadata access to an offline item recalls nothing.

The only writes to real share folders happen under mutant B inside scratch copies, against this user's own C: through loopback. M1's driver keeps that confined by construction.
